# NIST SD04 regression fixtures

This collection contains two impressions of each of ten fingerprints from
**NIST Special Database 4**, by Craig I. Watson, National Institute of Standards
and Technology. The source database contains 2,000 pairs spanning arch, left
loop, right loop, tented arch, and whorl patterns.

Source: [NIST SD04 publication](https://www.nist.gov/publications/nist-special-database-4-nist-8-bit-gray-scale-images-fingerprint-image-groups).
The original database dates to 1992; the publication entry is dated 2008, and
these files come from NIST's later PNG distribution. Applicable terms and the
transformation notice are preserved in [NIST-DATA-NOTICE.txt](NIST-DATA-NOTICE.txt).

## Selection

Each class has an ordinary pair and a pair with a second classification in the
source History field and Appendix C. Cross-referencing describes classification
ambiguity rather than an assigned image-quality grade.

- Arch: `0005_03`; cross-referenced `0070_10` (tented arch).
- Left loop: `0003_10`; cross-referenced `0091_10` (tented arch).
- Right loop: `0002_05`; cross-referenced `0110_08` (tented arch).
- Tented arch: `0021_07`; cross-referenced `0008_10` (left loop).
- Whorl: `0010_01`; cross-referenced `0371_05` (right loop).

The `f` and `s` prefixes identify the first and second impressions of the same
fingerprint. Pairing uses the complete numeric identifier and finger suffix.
The originally proposed `0001_01` is an ordinary whorl shown in Appendix A;
`0371_05` supplies the intended cross-referenced whorl coverage.

## Contents and independent baselines

Every PNG is an unchanged source file verified against the supplied SD04 MD5
listing. Each `.gray8` contains exactly 262,144 decoded pixels: 512 × 512,
8-bit grayscale, top-left origin, nominal 500 ppi. All rows, including the bottom
white band, are retained. Resolution is supplied from dataset documentation;
the PNG files carry no resolution metadata. PNG decoding changes the container
representation while preserving every pixel value.

The sampling-resolution basis is **19.6850 pixels/mm**, nominally 500 ppi, in
the SD04 entry on printed page 84 of the
[1994 NIST data-products catalog](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/Legacy/SP/nistspecialpublication782-1994.pdf).

`manifest.json` records pairing, classes, finger positions, source paths and
history, hashes, decoder version, transformation details, and reference build
provenance. Source metadata hashes are recorded; demographic fields are not
part of the test model. `images.tsv` is the manifest's generated C-friendly
index. `scores.tsv` contains all 400 ordered image comparisons.

The `.xyt` files, full `.min` type reports, and score matrix were generated by original **NBIS 5.0.0
command-line tools**, built independently of the OpenPhysical wrapper. All
2,168 original C/header/template source files were checked byte-for-byte against
the official archive after building. Legacy compiler compatibility flags are
recorded in the manifest. A temporary, uncompressed IHEAD envelope supplies the
same raw pixels and explicit 500 ppi to MINDTCT. Default MINDTCT V2/NIST XYT and
default Bozorth3 settings are used, with no enhancement or score threshold.

The matrix includes **20 self-comparisons, 20 ordered paired-impression
comparisons, and 360 ordered comparisons between different fingers**. µnit
checks those category counts as well as every reference score. Different-finger
scores include nonzero values; applications apply their matching policy to the
raw score when deciding whether to accept a comparison.

µnit owns the complete extraction and 400-score oracle matrix. NUnit checks every
marshaled point against XYT and independently recorded RIG/BIF types, and compares
each paired workflow with its recorded ordered score. JSON and native input
projection round trips preserve all point fields.
The example program demonstrates image/template combinations and LINQ reuse.

## Reproduce

Use macOS or Linux for the independent reference build. Start from the official
[NBIS archive](https://nigos.nist.gov/nist/nbis/nbis_v5_0_0.zip), whose SHA-256 is
`0adf8ab0f6b0e4208de50ca00ba21d3d77112ecd66288757ddfed21f6bee92c3`.
From the repository root:

```sh
python -m pip install -r scripts/requirements-fixtures.txt
python scripts/build-nbis-reference.py --archive /path/to/nbis_v5_0_0.zip --output artifacts/sd04-reference-rebuild
python scripts/import-sd04.py --source /path/to/sd04 --reference-build artifacts/sd04-reference-rebuild --output artifacts/sd04-reimport
```

The reference build requires a new output directory. Importing into a separate
directory allows comparison with the committed collection before updating it.
PNG/raw/XYT/MIN and score hashes should agree. Compiler/platform receipts and import
dates describe each particular generation run.

The type reports can also be reproduced directly from the committed raw pixels,
without decoding the source PNGs again:

```sh
python scripts/import-sd04.py --refresh-reference-minutiae --reference-build artifacts/nbis-reference-sd04
```

This mode requires the exact recorded reference receipt and tool hashes, and
checks that newly extracted XYT matches before retaining the `.min` reports.
The RIG/BIF tokens come directly from MINDTCT output. Integrity validation checks
row ordinals and coordinate alignment between MIN and XYT before those rows
supply type expectations: XYT retains MIN x and uses image height minus MIN y.

Normal builds use committed fixtures offline. Their integrity check uses only
Python's standard library:

```sh
python scripts/import-sd04.py --verify
```

Run the managed example with the collection explicitly:

```sh
dotnet run --project examples/OpenPhysical.Biometrics.NBIS.Examples -c Release -- --sd04 tests/fixtures/sd04
```
